A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same human shopping behavior simulation study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching the extended results table and appendix examples across renumbering and pagination changes.

before.justification: v7 reports original evaluations of prompt-only and fine-tuned LLMs, reasoning ablations, action distributions, and error analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v8 retains those original empirical results and adds model evaluations and a reasoning ablation on OPeRA.

M1.justification: The simplified HTML inputs, browser action space, reasoning synthesis, masked next-token training objective, and reasoning-then-action generation remain unchanged. Section 3.3 newly documents a two-turn format with an end_of_rationale message; this clarifies implementation without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v8 adds OPeRA as a second evaluation dataset, described as containing 51 users, 692 shopping sessions, and 28,904 observation-action pairs. This substantially extends coverage beyond the original cohort, whose dataset is retained and named ShopCART. Both datasets concern online shopping; no new domain or persona-conditioned task is demonstrated.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds a comparator labeled Qwen2.5-70B while retaining every earlier comparator. The new OPeRA comparison also introduces GPT-4.1 and Llama-3.3-70B alongside retained model families. These are limited extensions of the existing pretrained-versus-fine-tuned comparison.

E3.justification: Table 1 extends the prompt-only Qwen configurations from 1.5B, 3B, and 7B to a reported 70B model. The stated session-held-out design, exact-match accuracy, session-outcome F1, and fine-tuning settings remain unchanged. OPeRA is described as repeating the setup, without specifying its actual split sizes.

E4.justification: The original reasoning ablations, action-distribution analysis, error categories, and search-revision examples are retained. New Table 2 extends the reasoning ablation to OPeRA, comparing fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B with and without reasoning traces.

E5.justification: The original McNemar tests and reported thresholds remain unchanged. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals, and the new OPeRA table introduces no additional uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: New OPeRA results include GPT-4.1 at 21.28% accuracy/51.17% F1 and fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B at 32.04%/71.38% without reasoning and 35.14%/75.85% with reasoning. Table 1 adds Qwen2.5-70B at 6.46%/11.96%. Existing table and figure values remain unchanged. Section 4.5 corrects 69.69% to 69.39%, and Section 5.2 corrects the reasoning-benefit finding from all models to most models, consistent with retained appendix exceptions.

T1.justification: The formal task mapping and action definitions are retained, with no new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical revision. The discussion of predictive versus cognitive reasoning is conceptual, and proposed alternative metrics are not formally developed.

C1.justification: The first introduction contribution changes from conducting the first process-centric evaluation to proposing ShopCART as the first process-centric evaluation dataset. The conclusion extends the fine-tuning finding to different datasets. The abstract's headline claims and original performance figures remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5 substantially expands interpretation: missing visual information may explain low accuracy; aggregate plausibility is distinguished from individual fidelity; and alternative metrics and application boundaries are specified. The existing synthetic-reasoning disclaimer gains application-specific discussion of human cognition. New limitations address proprietary-generation costs and difficulty evaluating the same reasoning-trained model in action-only mode. The shopping-only generalization limitation is retained.

D1.justification: v7 explicitly says the dataset cannot be released; v8 replaces this with a statement that code and data are available through the ShopCART link. This substantially changes reported resource access. v8 also specifies LLM-based personal-information removal, official APIs for proprietary models, and the two-turn generation delimiter. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, and appendix prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v8 adds citations including OPeRA, WebRL, CollabLLM, DPRF, and a human-agent collaboration platform, while removing the RPA evaluation survey citation. The related-work argument largely remains intact, with a limited shift toward positioning ShopCART as a named dataset contribution.

P1.justification: v8 makes localized wording corrections, updates authors and affiliations, introduces ShopCART terminology, and expands the discussion with a new Reasoning and Human Cognition subsection. The main section sequence and appendix content remain largely intact rather than undergoing a document-wide rewrite.

P2.justification: v8 adds the OPeRA table and a Table 1 row, restyles Figure 1 while preserving its illustrated pipeline, and places Figures 2 and 3 together. Existing example and appendix tables are renumbered and reflowed. The overall two-column design remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: The OPeRA evaluation provides additional support beyond the original cohort, while the reported ShopCART release and implementation disclosures improve reproducibility information. Expanded qualifications make the low accuracy and synthetic-reasoning findings easier to interpret. These gains are tempered by underspecified OPeRA splits and rationale handling, and by a new text-versus-vision argument based on success rates from different benchmarks rather than a controlled comparison.
